title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 7-12). L is a set. An 'admissible family' Φ ⊂ 𝔓(L) is a family of subsets satisfying axioms fixed on p. 7. From p. 12 these force ∅ ∉ Φ, and in fact A° ≠ ∅ for A ∈ Φ, which suggests a topological or 'figure' structure. F is the set of all admissible families, ordered by Φ ≤ Ψ iff Φ is an admissible ('closed') subfamily of Ψ. Closed subfamilies are essentially down-sets: for X ∈ Φ, Φ_X = {Y ∈ Φ | Y ⊆ X}.

Page 10 (C1): F admits sups of bounded-above families. If the Φ_i are closed subfamilies of a common Ψ, the union ∪Φ_i is again closed in Ψ and is the sup. The empty family is the least element.

This page:
(i) The irreducible elements of F are exactly the Φ that have a greatest element. A marginal note proposes calling them 'multiplicités' (or 'multiplicités irréductibles'). The justification is general order theory: a down-closed subset is irreducible (not a union of proper closed parts) iff it has a maximum. If Φ has no maximum, then Φ = ∪_X Φ_X with each Φ_X proper. If it has a maximum M, any covering family must contain M and so equals Φ.
(ii) C2: every Φ ∈ F is the sup of the irreducible elements below it, namely the Φ_X for X ∈ Φ.
(iii) C3: F, G ∈ F are compatible (= bounded above in F) iff every pair of multiplicities X ≤ F, Y ≤ G is compatible. Equivalently, F_X and G_Y are compatible for all X ∈ F, Y ∈ G. So compatibility is detected on irreducibles, in a binary, pairwise way.
(iv) Remark on condition 7 (compatibility of Φ, Ψ). This adds an equivalent condition d): for all A ∈ Φ and B ∈ Ψ, A∩B is 'formed' (closed) in A relative to Φ_A and in B relative to Ψ_B. Moreover, for C ⊆ A∩B one has C ∈ Φ iff C ∈ Ψ, i.e. Φ_{A∩B} = Ψ_{A∩B}.

This is a gluing/agreement-on-overlaps condition, exactly like compatibility of charts in an atlas or of local data to be glued. Purpose: build an 'algebra of figures' in which general figures are glued (as sups) from irreducible pieces ('multiplicités') along compatible overlaps. Page 12 then studies the connected components of the poset ℳ of multiplicities.

The resulting structure (bounded-complete poset, every element a sup of irreducibles/principal pieces, pairwise compatibility implies compatibility) is order-theoretically a coherent Scott-domain-like structure.
errors: C2 as transcribed says 'pour Y∈Φ'; it should be 'pour X∈Φ'.
The claim that Φ_X is itself an admissible closed subfamily (needed for C2) depends on the axioms of p. 7, which are not visible here. This is presumably justified there.
C3 (binary/pairwise compatibility suffices) is stated without proof on this page. It relies on the Cor. 3 / Scholie of pp. 7-10 and on condition d).

ideas.what: Irreducible (join-irreducible) closed subfamilies are exactly those with a greatest element; every element is the sup of its principal pieces Φ_X.
ideas.modern_name: Completely join-irreducible down-sets = principal down-sets; Alexandrov topology on a poset; algebraic/prime-generated lattice

ideas.what: Compatibility (existence of a common upper bound) of two families is detected pairwise on irreducible pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Coherence (binary consistency) in bounded-complete posets; coherent Scott domains, cf. Girard coherence spaces

ideas.what: Condition d): two admissible families are compatible iff on each overlap A∩B they induce the same family (Φ_{A∩B} = Ψ_{A∩B}) and A∩B is closed in both.
ideas.modern_name: Agreement on overlaps / atlas compatibility; gluing of combinatorial complexes along common subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (manifold atlases, sheaf gluing, cell-complex amalgamation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'algèbre des figures' organises figures as a bounded-complete poset generated by irreducible 'multiplicités', with binary (pairwise) compatibility. This is structurally a coherent Scott domain / coherence-space setup, contemporaneous with Girard's coherence spaces. The link between his combinatorial-geometric 'figures' and domain-theoretic coherence is not made in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour que F et G soient compatibles ... il faut et suffit que ∀ X ≤ F et Y ≤ G, multiplicités, on ait X et Y compatibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck independently arriving at domain-theoretic structures while building a combinatorial foundation for 'figures'. Mathematically the facts are elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary order-theoretic lemmas (principal down-sets as irreducibles, sup decomposition, pairwise compatibility) plus an agreement-on-overlaps criterion. It is interesting as part of an unpublished 1986 project on an 'algebra of figures' and for its coherence-domain flavour, but the results themselves are routine.
transcription_corrections: C2: 'pour Y∈Φ' should read 'pour X∈Φ'; the line reads 'Tout Φ∈F est le sup des objets irréductibles de F'.
C3: '(i.e. F, G [?])' is likely '(i.e. F, G majorés)', i.e. having a common upper bound.
Marginal note: 'Appelons-les multiplicités ou multiplicités irréductibles' (possibly 'multisets', cf. p. 12); placement in the margin next to lines 2-4.
Line 3-4 is probably 'un fermé est irréductible (dans un ensemble ordonné quelconque en fait) ssi il a un plus grand élément'; the exact wording is uncertain.
Remark d): 'A∩B est formé dans A' is plausibly 'est fermé dans A'.
